_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Ninja Gaiden (ADR-0239, PRD F14.16).
This file is data. A second game is a second file beside this one - no code
change - as long as its navigation address and every value it is set to are
read off a published RAM map or the vendored cheat database (ADR-0184 s5:
no code is invented). Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
Rung (ADR-0239 s1's ladder). Rung 2: a published RAM selector, pinned for
the run. Rung 1 was checked first and is not available for this ROM. The
game's only pure-input secret is the Sound Test - the vendored database
ships it as 'Sound test - hold down and press Start at Tecmo Presents
screen' - and it selects music, not a place. The hidden level select this
game is known for exists only behind Game Genie codes (US
AZUTYSXT+OTUVASXV+EGUVPSXT), which are PRG-space codes and refused outright
by ADR-0184 s1; the level select shown after the Act number screen is that
code's product, not a controller combination. There is no password system
in the US ROM. Rung 3 (a save state reached by search, chain or movie) is
out of this slice's scope and is not used here.
Selector and values. $006D is the game's current stage and $006E the current
room inside it (DataCrystal, 'Ninja Gaiden (NES)/RAM map': "$6D - The
current stage", "$6E - The current room - Stages can have multiple rooms").
$006D is a flat index over the game's 22 areas, 0x00 = Act 1-1 through
0x15 = Act 6-5. The vendored database enumerates it value by value
(006D:01 'Start on stage 1-2' ... 006D:15 'Start on stage 6-5 (final
boss)'), and Almar's Guides' Action Replay page lists the same 22 places
from 006D:00 = 1-1 to 006D:21 = 6-5 in decimal, which is the same sequence
written in the other base. Two published sources agree, and nothing here is
invented (ADR-0184 s5).
Every value was verified against the game's own HUD, not against the map
alone. One 20 s session per value, from power-on with this profile's entry
script and the pin in place, ends on a frame whose HUD reads STAGE-<act>-<area>
exactly as the value's title claims: 22 of 22 rows matched (contact sheet
runs/f1416/ninjagaiden/probe/shots/hud-22.png, unversioned), and the room
counter $006E is strictly increasing across the 22 values - 0, 1, 2, 6, 9,
is a fingerprint of the place the loader took, which is what each value's
ramCheck asserts.
0x00 (Act 1-1) is deliberately not a value of this sweep. Act 1-1 is what
the 'before' side of the measurement is (ADR-0239 s5 names the game's
current stage-1 route as before), and s4 scores a session that adds nothing
the baseline does not already hold as did-not-warp - a true statement about
a stage-1 session that would read as a failure in the table. The pin at
0x00 is instead the selector's own inertness control, measured below.
The stage-clear transition is never recorded by any session of this sweep:
the selector is pinned for the whole run, so the game never observes the
stage advancing (ADR-0184's 2026-09-14 amendment). Deaths and respawns are
still recorded - the blind body dies on most acts - so ADR-0184 s4 is met,
and the stage-1 route the baseline records ends in a death as it always did.

_inertnessComment: ADR-0239 s3 requires the profile's inert control to pass before a lives pin
may ride with a navigation pin; the same test is what ADR-0184's amendment
ran for Contra's $0030. Both halves were measured on this binary on
2026-09-26, same input script against the same run with no cheat, and
diff -rq over the whole textures/ tree:
1. The selector mechanism is inert. 006D:00 pinned from power-on, 20 s: 0 of
2048 internal-RAM bytes differ (scripts/mss_ram.py --diff). At the sweep's
own shape (this profile's entry + body repeated, 120 s) the pinned run and
the uncheated one are byte-identical - 0 of 627 files differ, and the two
final states are the same 006D=0 006E=0 0076=2 0065=16 0063=124. In the
60 s route shape (the minted stage-1 state, stage1-run.txt) the same pin
changes 436 of 563 files instead, because that run reaches the 1-1 -> 1-2
advance (stage1-run.txt's window 98) and a pinned selector correctly
refuses to observe it: the game's own $006D is left at $FF. That is the
caveat this profile's note above records - the stage-clear transition is
never recorded - and not a contamination.
2. The lives pin does NOT pass, so this profile carries none. $0076 is Ryu's
lives (DataCrystal and TASVideos RAM maps) and reads 2 in the minted
state, so 2 is the counter's start value. 0076:02 at the sweep's shape
differs from the uncheated run in 226 of 627 files of textures/, and the
pair that isolates it - the selector pin with the lives pin against the
selector pin alone - differs in exactly the same 226 files, while
[selector + lives] and [lives alone] are byte-identical to each other
(0 files). So the lives pin is what moves the tree, and ADR-0239 s3's
condition is a byte-identical tree. In the 60 s route shape it is 17 of
564 files. The pin does not even hold the counter it names: the pinned
run's own $0076 still ends at 1, because the cheat substitutes the byte on
the CPU read bus and leaves memory alone.
So no lives pin rides with this sweep, and the blind body is allowed to
die and to reach GAME OVER, which is what ADR-0184 s4 asks for. All four
arms are under runs/f1416/ninjagaiden/probe/controls/ (unversioned).

navigation.label: current stage
navigation.source: DataCrystal, Ninja Gaiden (NES)/RAM map: $6D is "The current stage" and $6E "The current room". The values are enumerated by the vendored cheat database (UI/Dependencies/Internal/CheatDb.Nes.json, Ninja Gaiden (USA), sha1 EAD83487D9BE2F1D16C1D0B438A361A06508CD85), which ships one 006D code per place: 006D:01 'Start on stage 1-2' through 006D:15 'Start on stage 6-5 (final boss)'. Almar's Guides' Action Replay stage-select page lists the same 22 places, 006D:00 = 1-1 to 006D:21 = 6-5, numbered in decimal. Published maps, cited per ADR-0184 s5.

_roomsComment: No rooms[] here, deliberately. scripts/stages/README.md defines that key as
the sessions a level selector cannot reach because it picks a level and not
a room inside one - Contra's bosses, which stay save-state sessions with no
cheat at all. $006D reaches all 22 of this game's areas, bosses included
(0x13 and 0x14 are the two Act 6-4 fights), so there is no place left over
for a room session. If a later slice needs a state inside a level, this is
where the README says it goes.
_ramCheckComment: Each value's ramCheck reads $006E off the session's final state and asks it
to be a room belonging to that place. The counter is deliberately not the
selector's address: a RAM cheat substitutes the byte on the CPU read bus and
leaves the byte in memory alone, so $006D itself reads 0 in the final state of
a warped run however far the pin went (measured on all 22 values, 2026-09-26,
and the same trap the sweep's own report warns about). $006E is the game's own
value with no pin on it, so the check says something the selector cannot.
The numbers are measured, not published, and a check is not a cheat, so
ADR-0184 s5's source rule does not reach them. What they say is that the room
counter is a running total over the whole game - 0 at 1-1, 1 at 1-2, 2 at 2-1,
6 at 2-2, 47 at 6-5 - which is why the expectations are not the flat stage
index. Each value expects two rooms: **the first room of its own place, or the
first room of the place before it**. The second is not slack - it was measured
and then explained by the game's own HUD. At the sweep's shape (entry + body
repeated, 120 s) 19 of the 21 values end on their own first room and two -
Act 3-3 and Act 4-4 - end one place back, $006E 0B and 11; a screenshot of each
of those two runs shows the HUD still reading STAGE-3-3 and STAGE-4-4, so the
counter was pushed back by the game's own "return to a previous room" logic
while the run stayed in the place the pin selected. Every one of the 21
measured finals is inside its expectation.
A run that never took the select reads the stage-1 room 00 or another place's
room, and a crash reads garbage; both are outside these sets and are reported
beside the tiles and the new count. Act 1-2's expectation is [01, 00] because
Act 1-1 has a single room, so that one row admits a never-warped value on the
check alone and has to be read together with its tiles.
_defaultsComment: The entry is the stage set's own mint script, unchanged, run as input rather
than as a state: a navigation session starts from power-on with the pin
already set, and the boot's own stage load is what the pin steers - measured
on all 22 values, each of which reaches its place with the timer at 147 (three
frames into the act) at 20 s. No save state is used, so nothing unversioned
has to travel with this profile.
The body is the stage set's own Act 1-1 route, repeated by
record_navigation_sweep.py until the 120 s budget is covered, exactly as
Contra's profile does (ADR-0184's amendment: effective input time, not the
cheat, is what moves the picture). It is a blind body on every act but its
own: it holds Right, slashes and hops, which is what the recorder needs (a
figure's cycle needs two turns of a hold) and not what clears a stage.
